title: fix(telegram): agent gets the same image twice when a reply re-sends the replied-to image
body:
> Maintainer update at `a23cbce82b`: the e2e test file, its harness additions and the test-lines allocation were replaced by a 3-row table in `bot.create-telegram-bot.native-pipeline.test.ts` (test lines −17 against main; production unchanged, +27/−3). Test Server userbot proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155273#issuecomment-6785042971. The test names and line counts in the Evidence section below describe the earlier heads.

Supersedes #126789. Related: #57278, #57280.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent receives the same Telegram image twice when a user replies to an image with that same image, because the current message and the reply ancestor are staged at different local paths.

## User Impact

User impact: a same-source image in a reply reaches the agent once instead of twice. A successfully downloaded current attachment claims its Telegram `file_unique_id`, so a reply ancestor or external reply with that id is not downloaded again. Distinct images and attachments without an id are unchanged. If the current download fails it claims nothing, so the replied-to copy still arrives next to the `[media unavailable: ...]` notice. Replies to images the bot sent keep delivering that image, as on `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram's `file_unique_id` is the stable source identity across file-id changes and local restaging. It is carried on the transient `TelegramMediaRef` from singleton ingress, album ingress, retained reply media and downloaded reply media, and checked at the current-media/reply-media join before a reply ancestor or an explicit external reply is hydrated. Since the merge in `1a7948f2ad71` that check lives in main's inline hydration path in `bot-handlers.message-pipeline.ts`.

Earlier heads also skipped reply media the bot had sent. That is gone: `main` hydrates it on purpose (`hydrates allowlisted group reply ancestors`), the bot's earlier image is context the user may be asking about, and ClawSweeper flagged the skip as P1. #57278 tracks the attribution proof and the reply-photo product decision; this PR does not close it.

No config, default, protocol, SQLite or persisted-schema change: `TelegramResolvedMedia.fileUniqueId` was already part of the persisted message-cache value, and the new optional field is on the transient ref. Six files, +390/-3.

## Evidence

Head `deaf739ab8d` merges main `401a1de38b9` (which contains #196432) into `b79ff0750d1`, with no conflicts. `b79ff0750d1` merged main `3855c896edd` into `1a7948f2ad7` and added `config/test-lines-allocations/155273-reply-media-source-identity.txt` (358). The diff against main is still the same 6 files, +390/-3, plus the allocation. None of main's 418 commits from `3855c896edd` to `401a1de38b9` touches any of those 7 files, so the measurements below against `3855c896edd` hold for `401a1de38b9` too.

Measured 2026-11-10, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1:

- `bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts` with Vitest on Node (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`): 4 passed (4), at `b79ff0750d1` and again at `deaf739ab8d`.
  - sends one provider image when the current and replied messages stage one source at different paths
  - keeps the unavailable-media notice and the replied copy when the current download fails
  - drops a reply ancestor whose source is already an attachment of the replying album
  - dedupes a same-source external reply against the current media
- Same tests with main's 4 production files at `3855c896edd`: 3 failed, 1 passed. The same-source reply gives `expected { payloads: 2, unique: 1 } to deeply equal { payloads: 1, unique: 1 }`; the album turn gets the replied original as an extra media path; the external reply calls `getFile` once. The unavailable-media case passes on `main` by design: it guards against over-deduping.
- CI's baseline ratchets in PR form at `deaf739ab8d` (`check:baseline-ratchets --base 401a1de38b9 --no-merge-base` with `RATCHET_PR_HEAD_SHA`): 10 of 10 ok, including line-cap ("6 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth") and test lines (`Test lines OK: 6629034; ceiling: 6629035; slack: 1.`). The allocation is the PR's net test-line growth, 358: at `b79ff0750d1` against `3855c896edd`, 359 was refused ("Test line allocation credit 359 exceeds allowed ceiling growth 358").
- `tsgo:all` passes. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the 6 changed files. `check:changed --base 3855c896edd` passes every stage except `changelog attributions`, which flags `Thanks @steipete-oai` and `Thanks @roboclaw-bot` lines in main's own `CHANGELOG/` files; this PR does not touch `CHANGELOG/`.
- Test cost, `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on the local default runtime (Bun): 58.3 s wall with a cold worker cache (46.6 s Vitest duration, 77% transform) and 25.2 s warm (13.5 s), 6.2 s and 6.0 s of tests. CI run 42751354682 (`checks-node-changed`, Bun shard): 88.9 s duration, 81% transform, 9.9 s of tests.

CI on `b79ff0750d1` (run 42754603539) failed only on test lines, `over by: 12; net delta: +358`, which was main's own overage at `ea3eb71a0263`. #196432 fixed it, and on `deaf739ab8d` (run 42834009838) `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passes with `Test lines OK: 6629073; ceiling: 6629074; slack: 1.` In the same run 32 jobs pass, including `checks-node-changed`, where the e2e file passes 4 of 4 (Bun shard: 68.9 s duration, 80% transform, 10.3 s of tests).

Two QA smoke jobs fail on that run, and `ci-gate` fails because they do. `QA Smoke CI (profile 2/6)` fails `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` and `profile 3/6` fails `subagent-empty-completion-recovery`, both with `timed out after 60000ms; final bus-event kinds=[inbound-message,outbound-message,outbound-message]`. Main fails both the same way. Built the way CI builds them (`OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build qaRuntime`, then `openclaw qa run --qa-profile smoke-ci --scenario <id>`, one scenario per run), on macOS arm64 with Node 26.12.1, both scenarios fail in 2 of 2 runs on main `401a1de38b9` and in 2 of 2 on `deaf739ab8d`, with the same message as CI. The control, `telegram-status-command`, passes 2 of 2 on both. Filed as #196899: the two scenarios first fail at `e230abd098e` (#196570), whose parent passes them 2 of 2.

- Through a real Gateway: the Telegram plugin, a loopback Bot API, and the scripted mock OpenAI provider, whose `/debug/requests` gives the final provider request of each turn. One DM, 5 turns, run twice on this head and twice on main `3855c896edd`. The Gateway logs `native runtime: {"node":"26.12.1", ...}` with no Bun entry in every run. Images in the final request's user turn:

  | Turn | main | this head |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Photo A | 1 | 1 |
  | Reply to A that re-sends A (new `file_id`, same `file_unique_id`) | 2, identical bytes | 1 |
  | Reply to A with a distinct photo B | 2 (B and A) | 2 (B and A) |
  | Text reply to a photo the bot sent (C) | 1 (C) | 1 (C) |
  | Reply to the bot's photo that re-sends C | 2, identical bytes | 1 |

  Both runs of each build gave the same counts. In the same-source turns the Bot API sees `getFile` and a download only for the new copy's `file_id` on both builds; on `main` the replied original comes back from the message cache as a second attachment with the same bytes. The same-source turn, from the run output (image hashes are sha256 prefixes of the image data):

  ```
  main:      SAME-SOURCE-REPLY {"finalRequestImages":2,"uniqueImages":1,"imageHashes":["2a2016c02648","2a2016c02648"],"botApi":["getFile:user-photo-a2","download:user-photo-a2","sendChatAction","sendMessage"]}
  this head: SAME-SOURCE-REPLY {"finalRequestImages":1,"uniqueImages":1,"imageHashes":["2a2016c02648"],"botApi":["getFile:user-photo-a2","download:user-photo-a2","sendChatAction","sendMessage"]}
  ```

  The Bot API is a local stand-in, so the harness assigns the matching `file_unique_id` values; the real Telegram run below shows a real re-sent copy keeping its id. The harness is not committed.

- On real Telegram (2026-11-10, a throwaway bot's DM, photos sent from my phone's gallery, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). One isolated Gateway per build, with its Bot API traffic through a local recorder that logs each update's photo `file_unique_id`s and each `getFile`, and the scripted mock provider recording every provider request. Images are counted in the final request's current user turn, as sha256 prefixes of the image data:

  | Turn | main `401a1de38b9` | this PR (`b79ff0750d1`) |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Photo A | 1 | 1 |
  | Reply to A that re-sends A from the gallery | 2, identical (`3cf05d55ac08` twice) | 1 (`3cf05d55ac08`) |
  | Reply to A with a distinct photo B | not run | 2 (`0b1374e73e32`, `3cf05d55ac08`) |

  Telegram kept the re-sent copy's identity: on both builds the reply's largest size is `AQADlw1rGyj9oEd-`, the same `file_unique_id` as photo A, and all 4 photo sizes match. It also returned the same `file_id`, so `getFile` ran once per turn for that file. From the recorder and the mock provider, this PR's same-source turn:

  ```
  q1 photo A           message 65  file_unique_id AQADlw1rGyj9oEd-  getFile AQADlw1rGyj9oEd-  final request images: 1 [3cf05d55ac08]
  q2 reply to 65, same message 67  file_unique_id AQADlw1rGyj9oEd-  getFile AQADlw1rGyj9oEd-  final request images: 1 [3cf05d55ac08]
  q3 reply to 65, B    message 69  file_unique_id AQADmQ1rGyj9oEd-  getFile AQADmQ1rGyj9oEd-  final request images: 2 [0b1374e73e32, 3cf05d55ac08]
  ```

  Why `b79ff0750d1` and not this head: its 7 files are byte-identical to this head's (`deaf739ab8d` only merges main, which touched none of them), and it predates main's `e230abd098e` (#196570). On this head, in an earlier run the same evening, the second and third photo turns logged `native vision support check failed: Error: Plugin invocation scope is closed`, and the current photo reached the model as an image description instead of an attachment: the same-source reply still carried one copy of A, not two, but as text. That comes from main, not this PR: in loopback runs with the native catalog wait forced to 300 ms, the same closed-scope throw appears 16 times per run on main `401a1de38b9` and on this head (2 of 2 runs each), and 0 times on `b79ff0750d1` (2 of 2). The throw is `assertOpen` in `src/plugins/plugin-invocation-scope.ts`, reached through the lazy binding `e230abd098e` added, the commit #196899 traces its QA failures to; here it arrives through the media-understanding vision check, not subagent delivery.

The e2e test mocks Telegram transport and assigns source ids, then calls the real image loader directly. Its image count is loader output, not a captured final provider request.

## Production observations (retained data to 2026-10-16)

**1. The duplicate case has not happened in production.** The two gateways' retained Telegram message caches (2026-09-15 to 2026-10-16) hold 281 inbound messages that carry media and reply to another message. 45 of them reply to a message that itself carries media. In 0 of those 45 does the current media share a `file_unique_id` with the replied-to media, so no production turn exists where this dedupe fired. This is a property of the incoming Telegram messages as stored, not of the build that received them.

**2. Source ids repeat across inbound updates.** On the gateway with 3 Telegram accounts, 18 photo `file_unique_id`s each appear on 2 to 4 separate messages: 38 messages, all from human senders, none forwarded; 5 of the 18 appear in two different chats. Documents and videos repeat the same way: 12 ids across 50 non-forwarded messages. Which client action produced each copy is not visible; a re-encoded copy would be a new file with a new id.

**3. A reply to an image the bot sent still carries that image into the turn.** Two turns on v2026.10.1 with local patches; in that build's four source files every line this PR adds or removes is added or removed the same way, the build's other local patches touch the same files elsewhere, and `bot.media.reply-source-identity.e2e.test.ts` is byte-identical. On 2026-10-13/14 two DM replies on the 3-account gateway replied to images the bot had sent; in both the stored transcript lists two attachments, the current one and then the replied-to file.

- Sticker replying to a bot photo: the run recorded `imagesCount: 1`, and that image is the replied-to photo.
- Photo replying to a bot image sent as a document: the bot's image entered as a `document` attachment and was handled as a file ("Unsupported document format" with its local path), not as an image.

## Not shown yet

- Re-sending other ways than from the phone's gallery (forward without the sender's name, paste from Telegram Desktop). The gallery re-send kept the same `file_unique_id`; the others were not measured.
- A distinct-photo control on main on real Telegram; the loopback runs above cover it.
